messages:
maya: quick question about the "hydra" handshake for staged rollouts — thinking about an escrowed traffic pool + probe sidecar. TL;DR: sidecar vs central probe, opinions?

Dave: sidecar wins on locality and avoiding an extra network hop, but it fans out probes which can be noisy. also deploy/upgrade complexity.

jun: sidecar increases footprint on GPU nodes (memory/cpu). can we share a probe process across replicas instead of one per pod?

Sophia: tradeoffs: sidecar = faster failover and lower probe latency. central = easier to version probes and aggregate telemetry. also consider runtimes where sidecar can’t run (air-gapped).

maya: another axis is escrow_ttl and sticky routing. if we put requests into an escrow pool during cutover, how long do we hold slots? and do we preserve session affinity during slow switchover?

Dave: i'd keep escrow TTL short, like 3-10s to avoid long-held capacity slots. affinity via request hash (session_id or user_id) is simplest. avoid global sticky leases.

jun: big concern: KV cache invalidation when switching model variant. we must include variant_id in cache keys or we’ll get silent corruption of outputs.

Sophia: yes — include variant_id and rollout_epoch in all cache keys and in telemetry. expect cache miss spike on switchover; capture that in dashboards.

deploy-bot: [automated] canary rollout started: model redwood/large-v2 weights 0->10% at 2026-03-18T11:05Z :rocket:

maya: fallback ordering question — prefer local cheaper fallback (smaller quantized model) before remote/regional fallback?

Dave: yeah, prefer local degrade first to minimize cross-region latency and costs. but allow policy to escalate to regional or hosted fallback if local saturates or fails.

jun: propose a simple scoring function for choosing fallback target: score = latency_penalty*latency_ms + error_penalty*error_rate_pct + cost_penalty*cost_unit. pick lowest score under threshold.

Sophia: on telemetry/sampling: add per-request tags: route_id, variant_id, probe_result, fallback_reason, escrow_hold_time. sample golden prompts at 1 qps for canary to detect semantic regressions.

maya: config surface thought: we should expose a declarative rollout policy schema (yaml) that includes probes, escrow_ttl, affinity, fallback_chain and scoring weights. keeps runtime simple.

maya: example draft:
```yaml
rollout:
  name: small-weight-canary
  weights: {baseline: 90, canary: 10}
  probes:
    latency_slo_ms: 150
    error_rate_pct: 1
  escrow_ttl_s: 5
  affinity: session_key
  fallback_chain: [local_shallow, regional_standard, degrade_text_only]
```

jun: probe design: combine black/white health checks with "golden prompt" semantic checks. run golden prompts at a low QPS and treat semantic failures as a probe failure if they exceed threshold.

Sophia: also add a probe heartbeat metric and a rolling-window probe pass rate to the decision function. dashboards need to show escrow pool size and avg_hold_time.

maya: proposed runtime implementation options: 1) inline runtime logic (router handles escrow & scoring) 2) sidecar helper that negotiates escrow with router over gRPC 3) external escrow service that all routers call. pros/cons?

Dave: 1) fast but couples router to rollout logic. 2) sidecar splits responsibility and lets us iterate on probe heuristics without router restarts. 3) central service simplifies cross-router coordination but is a single point of failure and adds latency.

jun: my leaning is sidecar helper with a lightweight gRPC API: AcquireEscrow(route, session_key, desired_variant) -> granted|timeout|fail. sidecar can cache probe results and do golden evals.

Sophia: agree on sidecar but require a feature-flag path to central service for environments that cannot run sidecars (private/on-prem). keep the API stable.

maya: action items: sophia to draft rollout schema PR, jun to audit cache keys for variant_id + epoch tagging, dave to prototype sidecar probe resource usage on a small testbed. i'll wire this into the console telemetry docs.

ops-oncall: note for runbook: add step to "drain escrow pool" before force rollback and add automated alert if escrow pool growth > 2x baseline. :white_check_mark:

Sophia: will add dashboards and alert queries.

jun: i'll start a perf test to measure sidecar CPU/RAM at 1000 req/s per node.

maya: thanks all — feel free to push small PRs, i'll centralize the design doc in /docs/rollouts once initial PRs land. (react :eyes: by jun)
